items.followUp: Define energy and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Awards credit for defining work and including the direction condition.
rubric.description: Defines work as the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force.
rubric.how: Check that the answer relates force and displacement and specifies the direction of the force.

rubric.why: Awards credit for identifying the SI unit of work.
rubric.description: States that the SI unit of work is the joule (J).
rubric.how: Check for joule or its symbol, J.

modelAnswer: Work is the product of a force and the displacement produced in the direction of the force.
The SI unit of work is the joule (J).

items.followUp: What is a solar panel? State one use.

rubric.why: Awards credit for explaining what a solar cell does.
rubric.description: States that a solar cell converts sunlight or solar energy into electrical energy.
rubric.how: Check for the input energy and the electrical energy produced.

rubric.why: Awards credit for stating a practical use of solar cells.
rubric.description: Gives a valid use, such as providing electrical power in artificial satellites.
rubric.how: Check that at least one practical application is named.

modelAnswer: Solar cells are devices that convert sunlight directly into electrical energy.
They are used to provide electrical power in artificial satellites.

items.followUp: Define one kilowatt and express it in watts.

rubric.why: Awards credit for defining a watt.
rubric.description: Defines one watt as the rate of doing one joule of work per second.
rubric.how: Check for the relationship 1 W = 1 J/s or an equivalent verbal definition.

rubric.why: Awards credit for naming the larger units requested.
rubric.description: Names kilowatt and megawatt as larger units of watt.
rubric.how: Check that both kilowatt and megawatt are named.

modelAnswer: Watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second.
Larger units of watt include kilowatt (kW) and megawatt (MW).

items.followUp: A mass of 300 g occupies a volume of 150 cm³. Find its density in kg/m³.

rubric.why: Awards credit for converting both given quantities to SI units.
rubric.description: Converts the mass to 0.5 kg and the volume to 2 × 10^-4 m³.
rubric.how: Check that both SI values are correct.

rubric.why: Awards credit for using the density relation and obtaining the correct result.
rubric.description: Calculates density as 2500 kg/m³ using mass divided by volume.
rubric.how: Check for the density relation or its substitution, and the correct answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: mass, m = 500 g = 0.5 kg; volume, V = 200 cm^3 = 2 × 10^-4 m^3.
Formula: density, ρ = m/V.
Substitution: ρ = 0.5 kg ÷ (2 × 10^-4 m^3).
Answer: ρ = 2500 kg/m^3.

rubric.why: Awards credit for using the correct Fahrenheit-to-Celsius relation.
rubric.description: Uses C = (F − 32) × 5/9 or an equivalent form.
rubric.how: Check that the Fahrenheit temperature is reduced by 32 and multiplied by 5/9.

rubric.why: Awards credit for the correct conversion result.
rubric.description: Obtains approximately 37.8°C.
rubric.how: Check for a correct Celsius value with its unit.

modelAnswer: Given: temperature, F = 100°F.
Formula: C = (F − 32) × 5/9.
Answer: 100°F ≈ 37.8°C.

items.followUp: Derive the third equation of motion using a speed-time graph.

rubric.why: Awards credit for interpreting displacement from the speed-time graph.
rubric.description: States that displacement is represented by the area under the speed-time graph.
rubric.how: Check for the connection between the area under the graph and displacement.

rubric.why: Awards credit for finding the trapezium area under the graph.
rubric.description: Writes displacement as s = 1/2(u + v)t.
rubric.how: Check for the correct area expression using initial speed, final speed and time.

rubric.why: Awards credit for using the first equation of motion in the derivation.
rubric.description: Uses v = u + at to relate initial speed, final speed, acceleration and time.
rubric.how: Check for the correct first equation of motion.

rubric.why: Awards credit for reaching the second equation of motion.
rubric.description: Derives s = ut + 1/2 at².
rubric.how: Check that the final equation is correct.

modelAnswer: Displacement s is the area under the speed-time graph.
The area is that of a trapezium: s = 1/2(u + v)t.
From the first equation of motion, v = u + at, so t = (v − u)/a.
Substituting for v in s = 1/2(u + v)t gives s = 1/2(u + u + at)t.
Therefore, s = ut + 1/2at^2, the second equation of motion.

items.followUp: Two perpendicular forces of 6 N and 8 N act on an object. Find the magnitude and direction of their resultant.

rubric.why: Awards credit for recognizing the geometry of the components.
rubric.description: Identifies the force components as perpendicular.
rubric.how: Check for a statement that the components act at 90° or are perpendicular.

rubric.why: Awards credit for the Pythagorean relation between the components and resultant.
rubric.description: Relates the resultant and its perpendicular components using Pythagoras' theorem.
rubric.how: Check for the squared-component relation.

rubric.why: Awards credit for the resultant's magnitude formula.
rubric.description: Gives the magnitude as the square root of the sum of the squares of the components.
rubric.how: Check for the correct magnitude formula.

rubric.why: Awards credit for the direction relation.
rubric.description: Gives the relation for finding the resultant's direction from the components.
rubric.how: Check for the correct component ratio or its inverse-tangent form.

modelAnswer: Let the perpendicular force components be Fx and Fy.
The resultant force R is the diagonal of the right-angled triangle formed by the components.
By Pythagoras' theorem, R^2 = Fx^2 + Fy^2.
Therefore, the magnitude is R = sqrt(Fx^2 + Fy^2).
If θ is measured from Fx, its direction is given by tan θ = Fy/Fx, so θ = tan^-1(Fy/Fx).

items.followUp: A person pushes a box with a force of 200 N through 30 m in 20 s. Find the power used.

rubric.why: Awards credit for correctly identifying the given quantities.
rubric.description: Identifies the force, displacement and time.
rubric.how: Check for 300 N, 50 m and 60 s.

rubric.why: Awards credit for the relation used to calculate work.
rubric.description: Uses work = force × displacement.
rubric.how: Check for W = Fd or its verbal equivalent.

rubric.why: Awards credit for calculating the work done.
rubric.description: Calculates work as 15 000 J.
rubric.how: Check for the correct substitution and work value with unit.

rubric.why: Awards credit for the relation used to calculate power.
rubric.description: Uses power = work/time.
rubric.how: Check for P = W/t or its verbal equivalent.

rubric.why: Awards credit for the correct final power.
rubric.description: Obtains a power of 250 W.
rubric.how: Check for the correct numerical answer with watt as the unit.

modelAnswer: Given: force, F = 300 N; displacement, d = 50 m; time, t = 60 s.
Formula for work: W = Fd.
Substitution: W = 300 N × 50 m = 15 000 J.
Formula for power: P = W/t.
Substitution: P = 15 000 J ÷ 60 s = 250 W.
Answer: The power used is 250 W.
